# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 36 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 36 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_036_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 6, Chapter 2 — How to Discern the Two Angels

**1** "Sir, how do I tell which spirit is from God and which is from the devil?" **2** "I'll give you a description of both," he said. "Test them against what I tell you. **3** The spirit from God is patient, peaceful, modest — it stays away from all wickedness and all the empty desires of this world. It humbles itself before everyone. It stays quiet. It doesn't pick fights. It doesn't push itself to the front. It doesn't speak boldly or forcefully — when it speaks, it speaks through peace and gentleness. **4** This spirit has God's approval. So when this spirit is active in your heart, speak with it about righteous things. Because where the Lord lives, deception has no place. Where God is, great understanding is also present. Trust the spirit from God — it has real power. Give no trust at all to the spirit from the devil — it has none. **5** What exactly is the power of the spirit from God, and what is the power of the one from the devil?" **6** "The spirit from the devil has no power at all," he answered. "It's as weak as dead winter grass — foolish and untrustworthy. When this earthly spirit has no power, it's like a withered vegetable in winter — it dries up and blows away. **7** But the spirit from God has real life in it — vigorous and strong, with genuine character. It's completely trustworthy, no wavering. When this spirit is in your heart, speak with it about righteousness, justice, and holiness."

---

*PNEUMA note: The contrast of winter grass (dead, powerless, temporary) with the vigorous divine spirit (full of life, strong) is a beautiful pastoral image — the demonic has no real substance; only the divine has genuine life-power.*
